brief: One drawer and one spike, both at the very same corner of the same cell, touching.

requirements.requirement: One drawer at a corner of a cell
requirements.evidence: notch:0#1,1#notch2 (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf) placed in empty cell 1,1 k=2 between pieces 0,1,0 and 1,0,0

requirements.requirement: One spike at the very same corner of the same cell as the drawer
requirements.evidence: spike:0#0,0|0,1|1,0 is the only spike site offered for this 3-cell L. Configurator requires 3 occupied cells for a spike and an empty cell for a notch, so they cannot occupy the identical junction coordinate. Spike is on the same two cells (0,1,0 and 1,0,0) but at the opposite corner of those cells (junction 0,0|0,1|1,0 vs 0,1|1,0|1,1)

Both parts flank cell 1,0,0 and 0,1,0; meshClash clear with no clash, caps and joints locked. Visual top view shows L of 3 bases with spike in inner corner and drawer frame filling the outer V, bodies adjacent.

finish.summary: Built 3 full bases in L (0,0,0; 0,1,0; 1,0,0) with the only available spike at inner junction 0,0|0,1|1,0 and a notch drawer frame in the complementary empty cell 1,1. Configurator rules prevent spike and notch sharing the exact same junction coordinate (spike needs 3 filled cells, notch needs 1 empty), so they are placed on the same two cells at adjacent corners, as close and touching as the system allows.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
